definitions.title: Three-Dimensional Cartesian Coordinate System
definitions.statement: A three-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system is formed by three mutually perpendicular directed coordinate axes (the x-, y-, and z-axes) meeting at a single origin point (0, 0, 0) and satisfying the right-hand rule.
definitions.explanation: Every point in Euclidean 3-space is identified with a unique ordered triplet of real numbers representing signed distances from coordinate planes.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Extends Cartesian plane geometry to physical 3D space via three coordinate planes: xy, yz, and xz.

definitions.title: Distance Formula and Standard Equation of a Sphere
definitions.statement: The Euclidean distance between P_1(x_1, y_1, z_1) and P_2(x_2, y_2, z_2) derives from double application of the Pythagorean theorem. A sphere of radius a centered at (h, k, l) is the locus of points at distance a from (h, k, l).
definitions.explanation: Completing the square in quadratic 3D equations reveals the center and radius of spheres or determines if the locus is degenerate.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Spheres generalize 2D circles into 3D through equal distance from a central locus.
